page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7.6xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage, meaning all storage operations must rely on external network-attached volumes. Network connectivity is supported by a 12 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the average tier for most compute and memory operations. The Intel Xeon processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. In testing, the instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 1534.0 and a multi-core score of 11384.0. Memory bandwidth tests recorded 129.12 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 62.93 GB/sec for write operations. Notably, the instance demonstrated strong performance in text generation for small language models, reaching 283.7 tokens per second, though performance scales down to 14.18 tokens per second for medium 7B models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.r7.6xlarge offers a dense memory allocation relative to its CPU core count, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require local high-speed SSDs. The lack of bundled local storage represents a clear tradeoff, requiring users to factor in the cost and latency of network storage. This instance is well-suited for workloads such as in-memory databases like Redis, where it achieved 23.5 million operations per second in benchmark testing, as well as enterprise applications, caching layers, and moderate data processing tasks.
